name: Joshua
overview: Joshua was a male from the tribe of Ephraim, known primarily as one of the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan, originally named Hoshea. He served as an assistant to Moses and played a significant role in Israel's history as a faithful leader from Ephraim. His unique distinction includes being one of the spies who trusted God’s promise of victory.
namesAndTitles: Joshua means 'YHWH saves,' reflecting God's saving power, while his original name Hoshea means 'salvation.' Both names highlight the theme of deliverance and trust in God, underscoring his role as a divinely appointed leader.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Joshua was the son of Nun. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are noted in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Joshua is significant in the biblical narrative as Moses' servant and successor who led the Israelites into the Promised Land. His faithfulness as one of the twelve spies who trusted God’s promise set him apart, enabling him to lead the conquest of Canaan. His leadership prefigures Christ as the one who guides God's people into their spiritual inheritance and rest.

keyEvents.event: Led Israel in battle against Amalek
